preamble: Backing and rounding the nucleus of the PRICE diphthong /aɪ/ toward [ɒɪ ~ ɔɪ] is a well-known feature of broad urban accents of English. In Cockney, /aɪ/ is usually [ɑɪ], but in 'vigorous, dialectal' Cockney it is [ɒɪ] (Wells 1982). Broad Australian English likewise rounds and raises the first element, giving [ɒːe]. Because the rounded realizations stay on the broad end of the accent continuum, the change is mostly regional.

examples.note: Wells gives Cockney PRICE as [ɑɪ], or even [ɒɪ] in broad speech. The vowel can approach CHOICE without fully merging with it.
In broad accents the first element of PRICE is raised and rounded (Wells 1982: 597; Harrington, Cox & Evans 1997).

sources: Wells, J. C. (1982). Accents of English. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511611759
